tldr: vLLM announced day-0 support for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on Oct 15, covering image, document and video input through OpenAI-compatible serving. Comparison write-ups against rival open models followed within a day.
whats_new: OrcaRouter published head-to-head comparisons on Oct 16 pitting Nemotron 3.5 Super VL against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp, framed around pricing and availability rather than raw scores.
why_it_matters: Day-0 vLLM support means you can test Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on an existing OpenAI-compatible serving stack for document and video agents; the comparisons show the real decision is metered API versus self-hosted weights.

status.detail: Servable on vLLM from launch day; independent comparisons started appearing Oct 16.

beats.headline: vLLM ships day-0 support for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
beats.summary: Multimodal serving (image, document, video) with OpenAI-compatible endpoints and multi-token prediction.

beats.headline: OrcaRouter pits it against Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp
beats.summary: Three write-ups in one day, centered on metered pricing versus downloadable weights.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks confirm the index-point gaps OrcaRouter reports against DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp?
Will other inference engines or clouds add Nemotron 3.5 Super VL beyond vLLM?
take_for_builders: If you run multimodal document or video agents, point an existing vLLM deployment at Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and rerun your own eval before trusting a single vendor-neutral comparison site.
